title: Psalms Chapter 119 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 119 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 119 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 119.

questions.question: In Psalms 119, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Blessed are the undefiled in the way
I have chosen the way of truth
questions.correctAnswer: Blessed are the undefiled in the way
questions.explanation: This is stated in the very first verse of the chapter, Psalms 119:1.

questions.question: What is said about those who keep the testimonies of the Lord?
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:2 states that 'Blessed are they that keep his testimonies...'

questions.question: According to Psalms 119, what do the undefiled do?
options: They walk in the law of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: They walk in the law of the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:1 states that the undefiled are those who walk in the law of the LORD.

questions.question: What does the psalmist ask for in Psalms 119:18?
options: To behold wondrous things out of the law
questions.correctAnswer: To behold wondrous things out of the law
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:18 asks for God to open the psalmist's eyes to behold wondrous things out of His law.

questions.question: What is said about the proud in Psalms 119:21?
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:21 states that 'Thou hast rebuked the proud that are cursed...'

questions.question: What does the psalmist declare with his lips according to Psalms 119:13?
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:13 mentions that 'With my lips have I declared all the judgments of thy mouth.'

questions.question: What does the psalmist desire to do with his whole heart according to Psalms 119:10?
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:10 states, 'With my whole heart have I sought thee...'

questions.question: According to Psalms 119:24, what are the testimonies of the Lord to the psalmist?
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:24 states, 'Thy testimonies also are my delight and my counsellors.'

questions.question: What does the psalmist ask for in Psalms 119:39?
options: To have his reproach turned away
questions.correctAnswer: To have his reproach turned away
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:39 states, 'Turn away my reproach which I fear...'

questions.question: What does the psalmist say he will do with his hands in Psalms 119:48?
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:48 states, 'My hands also will I lift up unto thy commandments...'

questions.question: What has the psalmist hid in his heart according to Psalms 119:11?
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:11 states, 'Thy word have I hid in mine heart, that I might not sin against thee.'

questions.question: Is it true that the psalmist rejoices in the way of the Lord's testimonies?
questions.explanation: The psalmist states in Psalms 119:14, 'I have rejoiced in the way of thy testimonies...'

questions.question: Is it true that the psalmist wants to understand the way of God's precepts?
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:27 expresses the desire to understand the way of God's precepts.

questions.question: Is it true that the psalmist claims he will not keep the law?
questions.explanation: The psalmist expresses his intent to keep the law throughout Psalms 119, such as in verse 44.

questions.question: Is it true that the psalmist has forgotten the word of the Lord?
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:16 states, 'I will not forget thy word,' indicating he remembers it.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 119 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 119 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did the psalmist do without delay regarding God's commandments?
options: I made haste, and delayed not to keep thy commandments.
questions.correctAnswer: I made haste, and delayed not to keep thy commandments.
questions.explanation: The psalmist expressed urgency in obeying God's commandments in Psalms 119:60.

questions.question: What promise is made in Psalms 119:61 about remembering God's law?
options: The bands of the wicked will not rob me.
I will be rewarded for my remembrance.
I will not forget thy law.
I will be free from affliction.
questions.correctAnswer: I will not forget thy law.
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:61 states that despite the wicked's actions, the psalmist has not forgotten God's law.

questions.question: At what time does the psalmist rise to give thanks?
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:62 indicates that the psalmist rises at midnight to give thanks because of God's righteous judgments.

questions.question: What does the psalmist identify as a source of companionship?
questions.explanation: According to Psalms 119:63, the psalmist is a companion of those who fear the Lord and keep His precepts.

questions.question: What does the psalmist ask God to teach him in Psalms 119:64?
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:64 shows the psalmist requesting God to teach him His statutes, recognizing the earth is full of God's mercy.

questions.question: What benefit does the psalmist attribute to being afflicted?
options: It helped him learn God's statutes.
questions.correctAnswer: It helped him learn God's statutes.
questions.explanation: In Psalms 119:71, the psalmist states that it is good he was afflicted because it led him to learn God's statutes.

questions.question: What does Psalms 119:72 say is better than thousands of gold and silver?
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:72 emphasizes that the law of God's mouth is more valuable than vast riches.

questions.question: What was the psalmist's response to the proud who forged lies against him?
questions.explanation: The psalmist resolved to keep God's precepts wholeheartedly despite the lies of the proud, as stated in Psalms 119:69.

questions.question: What does the psalmist express a desire for in Psalms 119:77?
options: To have tender mercies come unto him
questions.correctAnswer: To have tender mercies come unto him
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:77 shows the psalmist asking for God's tender mercies so that he may live, as God's law is his delight.

questions.question: What does Psalms 119:79 say about those who fear God?
options: They will turn unto the psalmist.
questions.correctAnswer: They will turn unto the psalmist.
questions.explanation: In Psalms 119:79, the psalmist expresses hope that those who fear God will turn to him due to his understanding of God's testimonies.

questions.question: What does the psalmist declare about God's word in Psalms 119:89?
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:89 proclaims that God's word is forever settled in heaven, indicating its permanence and authority.

questions.question: What does Psalms 119:93 emphasize about the psalmist's relationship with God's precepts?
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:93 states the psalmist will never forget God's precepts, as they have brought him life.

questions.question: I have sworn to keep God's righteous judgments. (True/False)
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:106 shows that the psalmist has sworn to keep God's righteous judgments.

questions.question: The psalmist believes that his affliction is unjustified. (True/False)
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:75 indicates the psalmist acknowledges that God's judgments are right, even in affliction.

questions.question: The psalmist delights in God's law while being pursued by the wicked. (True/False)
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:70 reveals the psalmist delights in God's law despite the challenges he faces, indicating a consistent commitment.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 119 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 119.

questions.question: What does the psalmist love because of God's actions towards the wicked?
questions.explanation: The psalmist states in Psalms 119:119, 'Thou puttest away all the wicked of the earth like dross: therefore I love thy testimonies.' The love for God's testimonies is directly linked to His judgment of the wicked.

questions.question: How does the psalmist express his fear of God?
options: My flesh trembleth for fear of thee
My heart is filled with joy
questions.correctAnswer: My flesh trembleth for fear of thee
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:120 states, 'My flesh trembleth for fear of thee; and I am afraid of thy judgments.' This indicates a profound reverence and fear of God’s authority.

questions.question: What does the psalmist request regarding his oppressors?
options: Leave me not to mine oppressors
Make me a ruler over them
questions.correctAnswer: Leave me not to mine oppressors
questions.explanation: In Psalms 119:121, the psalmist implores God, 'I have done judgment and justice: leave me not to mine oppressors,' indicating his reliance on God for justice.

questions.question: What does the psalmist desire from God concerning understanding?
options: Give me understanding, that I may know thy testimonies
Teach me to forget my enemies
Allow me to be in confusion
questions.correctAnswer: Give me understanding, that I may know thy testimonies
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:125 states, 'I am thy servant; give me understanding, that I may know thy testimonies.' This reflects the psalmist's deep desire for wisdom from God.

questions.question: What does the psalmist love more than gold?
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:127 reveals, 'Therefore I love thy commandments above gold; yea, above fine gold.' This shows the value the psalmist places on God's commandments.

questions.question: What gives light and understanding to the simple according to the psalmist?
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:130 states, 'The entrance of thy words giveth light; it giveth understanding unto the simple,' indicating the illuminating power of God's word.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'precept' in Psalms 119:128 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'precept' in this context refers to a specific command or instruction from God, emphasizing the authority behind His word.

questions.question: What literary device is used in Psalms 119:164, 'Seven times a day do I praise thee'?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'Seven times a day' employs repetition to emphasize the psalmist's dedication to praising God throughout the day.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to Psalms 119:136, where the psalmist expresses sorrow for those who do not keep God's law?
questions.explanation: Romans 7:14-15 discusses the struggle between the desire to keep God's law and the reality of sin, paralleling the psalmist's anguish in Psalms 119:136.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to Psalms 119:165, which states, 'Great peace have they which love thy law'?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:3 promises peace to those whose minds are stayed on God, echoing the sentiment of peace found in loving God's law in Psalms 119:165.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Psalms 119:145?
options: Let my supplication come before thee
I have longed for thy salvation
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:146 directly follows verse 145, which states 'I cried unto thee; save me, and I shall keep thy testimonies.'

questions.question: What does the psalmist express in Psalms 119:150 when he says, 'They draw nigh that follow after mischief'?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'They draw nigh that follow after mischief' in Psalms 119:150 shows the psalmist's awareness of the threat posed by those who pursue evil.

questions.question: The psalmist's declaration that he has chosen God's precepts indicates a life of what?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 119:173, the statement 'for I have chosen thy precepts' signifies a deliberate choice to follow God's law, which reflects a life of obedience.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist feels he has gone astray like a lost sheep.
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:176 states, 'I have gone astray like a lost sheep; seek thy servant; for I do not forget thy commandments,' indicating his acknowledgment of straying.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist claims to have forgotten God's commandments.
questions.explanation: The psalmist affirms in Psalms 119:176, 'I do not forget thy commandments,' showing his commitment to remember God's law.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 119 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 119 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 119:6 teach about the believer's relationship to God's commandments?
options: Respect for all God's commandments prevents shame in the believer's life
God's commandments are optional and based on personal preference
The believer is justified by works of the law alone
Shame is inevitable despite obedience to God's law
questions.correctAnswer: Respect for all God's commandments prevents shame in the believer's life
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:6 states that the psalmist will not be ashamed when having respect unto all God's commandments, emphasizing a positive relationship between obedience and honor.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine teaching is emphasized in Psalms 119:12?
options: God is the teacher of His statutes, enabling the believer to learn and obey
Human wisdom is sufficient without divine instruction
The law is obsolete and replaced by human traditions
God commands but does not teach His statutes
questions.correctAnswer: God is the teacher of His statutes, enabling the believer to learn and obey
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:12 blesses God and requests teaching of statutes, showing God as the divine instructor who enables understanding and obedience.

questions.question: What doctrine regarding sanctification is taught in Psalms 119:33?
options: Divine teaching results in persevering obedience to God's statutes
Sanctification is independent of God's word
Obedience is achieved solely through human effort
God's statutes are a burden to the believer
questions.correctAnswer: Divine teaching results in persevering obedience to God's statutes
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:33 petitions God to teach the way of His statutes so the psalmist may keep it unto the end, illustrating sanctification through divine instruction and perseverance.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 119:89 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:89 declares that God's word is settled forever in heaven, highlighting the attribute of eternal faithfulness.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Psalms 119:64?
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:64 states 'The earth, O LORD, is full of thy mercy,' emphasizing God's merciful nature.

questions.question: How does Psalms 119:105 connect to the broader biblical theme of divine guidance?
options: It affirms God's word as a guiding light, preparing for Christ as the Light of the world
It denies the need for any divine guidance
It teaches that guidance comes only through human wisdom
It suggests darkness is preferable to following God's law
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms God's word as a guiding light, preparing for Christ as the Light of the world
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:105 calls God's word a lamp and light, which anticipates New Testament revelation of Christ as the true Light (John 8:12).

questions.question: In what way does Psalms 119:71 prepare for New Testament themes of suffering and sanctification?
options: Affliction is good for learning God's statutes, paralleling Christ's teaching on suffering producing holiness
Affliction is always a sign of divine abandonment
God's law is irrelevant during affliction
questions.correctAnswer: Affliction is good for learning God's statutes, paralleling Christ's teaching on suffering producing holiness
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:71 states affliction is good to learn statutes, resonating with New Testament teachings on suffering's sanctifying purpose (e.g., Romans 5:3-5).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 119:11 and Psalms 119:37 teach about the believer's spiritual warfare?
options: Hiding God's word in the heart and turning away from vanity protects against sin
Believers cannot overcome temptation through Scripture
Vanity is to be embraced as part of Christian life
questions.correctAnswer: Hiding God's word in the heart and turning away from vanity protects against sin
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:11 speaks of hiding God's word to avoid sin, and 119:37 requests turning eyes from vanity, together teaching Scripture's role in spiritual vigilance.

questions.question: What doctrine about hope and divine justice is taught by combining Psalms 119:81 and Psalms 119:84?
options: The believer longs for salvation and divine judgment against persecutors
Hope in salvation negates the need for justice
Divine justice is delayed and uncertain
Persecution proves God's rejection of the believer
questions.correctAnswer: The believer longs for salvation and divine judgment against persecutors
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:81 expresses fainting for salvation with hope in God's word; 119:84 asks when God will execute judgment on persecutors, jointly affirming hopeful expectation of God's justice.

questions.question: How do Psalms 119:67 and Psalms 119:71 together teach about the role of affliction in sanctification?
options: Affliction leads to repentance and learning God's statutes
Affliction causes abandonment of God's law
God's law is irrelevant in affliction
questions.correctAnswer: Affliction leads to repentance and learning God's statutes
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:67 recounts going astray before affliction, then keeping God's word; 119:71 says affliction is good to learn statutes, together teaching affliction's sanctifying purpose.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Psalms 119:85-88 promotes a fatalistic view of persecution with no hope. What does this passage actually teach?
options: It acknowledges wrongful persecution but calls for divine help and faithfulness to God's precepts
It encourages believers to give up in persecution
It denies the reality of persecution
It teaches that persecution is deserved because of sin
questions.correctAnswer: It acknowledges wrongful persecution but calls for divine help and faithfulness to God's precepts
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:85-88 describes enemies digging pits and wrongful persecution but asks God for help and affirms not forsaking God's precepts, showing hopeful faith amid trials.

questions.question: What doctrine about the believer's delight in God's law is taught in Psalms 119:16?
options: The believer delights in God's statutes and will not forget His word
The believer finds God's law burdensome and forgets it
Delight in God's law is optional and unimportant
God's word is inferior to human wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: The believer delights in God's statutes and will not forget His word
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:16 explicitly states the psalmist's delight in statutes and commitment not to forget God's word, teaching joy in divine law.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is illuminated by Psalms 119:158?
options: God's silence in times of grief
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:158 expresses grief over transgressors but implies God's righteous justice in dealing with them, highlighting divine justice.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about divine instruction and human response is taught by Psalms 119:73 and Psalms 119:125?
options: God's creation and teaching enable understanding of His commandments when the believer seeks diligently
Human intellect alone suffices to know God's law
Divine instruction is unnecessary for obedience
God does not respond to human requests for understanding
questions.correctAnswer: God's creation and teaching enable understanding of His commandments when the believer seeks diligently
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:73 acknowledges God as Creator giving understanding to learn commandments; 119:125 asks for understanding to know testimonies, teaching divine enabling upon seeking.

questions.question: How does Psalms 119:44 advance the narrative arc of perpetual obedience in the biblical covenantal framework?
options: It expresses a commitment to keep God's law forever, reflecting the covenantal promise of enduring obedience
It rejects obedience as temporary and insignificant
It suggests obedience is irrelevant to covenant relationship
It emphasizes obedience only for a limited time
questions.correctAnswer: It expresses a commitment to keep God's law forever, reflecting the covenantal promise of enduring obedience
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:44 declares continual obedience to God's law forever, resonating with covenant themes of enduring faithfulness to God's statutes.
